meta.title: Windows 11 commands: PowerShell and CMD cheatsheet
meta.description: Windows 11 commands cheatsheet: sfc, DISM, chkdsk, network, services, BitLocker, winget, with CMD or Linux equivalent and risk level.
meta.intro: Windows 11 troubleshooting and administration commands, in PowerShell and CMD. Each entry states its risk level: read-only, changes the system, or needs an elevated prompt (administrator).
meta.card: sfc, DISM, chkdsk, Get-Process, Get-WinEvent, Test-NetConnection, winget, BitLocker, gpupdate, robocopy: aliases, CMD/Linux equivalent, risk level.
meta.notice: Commands marked 'Needs admin' must be run in a terminal opened 'as administrator'. Read the description before running a command that changes the system.

entries.name: sfc /scannow
entries.desc: Checks protected system files and replaces corrupted ones.
entries.pitfall: If sfc fails, run DISM /RestoreHealth first and then run sfc again. Details are in %windir%\Logs\CBS\CBS.log.

entries.name: DISM /RestoreHealth
entries.desc: Repairs the running Windows image from Windows Update or a source.
entries.pitfall: The bar can sit at 20% or 62% for a long time: that is normal. PowerShell equivalent: Repair-WindowsImage -Online -RestoreHealth.

entries.name: chkdsk
entries.desc: Checks a volume's file system and fixes errors.
entries.pitfall: /f /r on the system volume requires a restart and can take hours. /scan (NTFS) works online.

entries.name: systeminfo
entries.desc: Shows the Windows version, hardware, memory, installed fixes and domain.
ex: systeminfo | findstr /B /C:"Nom de l'hôte" /C:"Nom du système d'exploitation"
entries.pitfall: The output depends on Windows' language; for scripts, prefer Get-ComputerInfo.

entries.name: Get-ComputerInfo
entries.desc: Detailed system information as a PowerShell object.
entries.pitfall: Without -Property, the command is slow (several seconds) because it collects everything.

entries.name: winver / Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem
entries.desc: Windows version and build.
entries.pitfall: Get-WmiObject no longer exists in PowerShell 7: use Get-CimInstance.

entries.name: hostname / Rename-Computer
entries.desc: Shows or changes the machine name.
entries.pitfall: On a domain-joined machine, add -DomainCredential.

entries.name: Restart-Computer / shutdown
entries.desc: Restarts or shuts down the machine, locally or remotely.
entries.perms: Shutdown rights (administrator for a remote machine)
entries.pitfall: shutdown /a cancels a scheduled shutdown as long as the delay has not elapsed.

entries.name: Get-HotFix
entries.desc: Lists installed fixes (KB).
entries.pitfall: Does not list all recent cumulative updates: complete with Get-WindowsUpdateLog or the Windows Update history.
entries.equiv: CMD: wmic qfe list; Linux: apt list --installed

entries.name: winget upgrade
entries.desc: Lists or installs updates for applications managed by winget.
entries.pitfall: Some applications need elevation; --include-unknown includes those whose version is not detected.

entries.name: winget install
entries.desc: Installs an application from the winget sources.
entries.pitfall: Use --id with -e (exact match) to avoid installing the wrong package.

entries.name: Get-WindowsUpdateLog
entries.desc: Generates a readable Windows Update log from the ETL traces.
entries.pitfall: Logs are in ETL format since Windows 10: without this command, WindowsUpdate.log is empty.

entries.name: usoclient / wuauclt
entries.desc: Triggers update scan or installation from the command line (not officially documented).
entries.pitfall: No output or error return: check in Settings > Windows Update. wuauclt /detectnow no longer works.

entries.name: Get-ChildItem
entries.desc: Lists files and folders, optionally recursively.
entries.pitfall: -Force also shows hidden and system files; -Filter is faster than -Include.

entries.name: Get-Item
entries.desc: Reads a file, folder or registry key (properties, attributes, dates).
entries.pitfall: For a file's content, use Get-Content, not Get-Item.

entries.name: Get-Content
entries.desc: Reads a text file, including continuous follow (like tail -f).
entries.pitfall: On a large file, avoid loading everything: use -Tail or -ReadCount.

entries.name: Select-String
entries.desc: Searches for a pattern in files or a stream (PowerShell grep).
entries.pitfall: The pattern is a regular expression: escape dots or use -SimpleMatch.

entries.name: robocopy
entries.desc: Robust folder copy (resume, multithread, mirror, permissions).
entries.pitfall: /MIR deletes at the destination whatever no longer exists at the source: always test with /L (dry run) first. Return codes 0 to 7 are successes.

entries.name: Copy-Item / Move-Item / Remove-Item
entries.desc: Copies, moves or deletes files and folders.
entries.pitfall: Add -WhatIf before any Remove-Item -Recurse: it does not go through the recycle bin.
entries.equiv: CMD: copy, move, del; Linux: cp, mv, rm

entries.name: icacls
entries.desc: Shows or changes the NTFS permissions of a file or folder.
entries.pitfall: Without (OI)(CI), the permission is not inherited by subfolders. /reset /T resets the whole tree.

entries.name: Get-Acl
entries.desc: Reads the permissions of a file, folder or registry key.

entries.name: Get-Process
entries.desc: Lists running processes (memory, CPU, path).
entries.pitfall: For a process's path or command line, use Get-CimInstance Win32_Process.
entries.equiv: CMD: tasklist; Linux: ps aux, top

entries.name: Stop-Process / taskkill
entries.desc: Terminates a process.
entries.pitfall: /T also terminates child processes. Terminating a system process can cause a blue screen.

entries.name: tasklist
entries.desc: Lists processes with, optionally, the services they host.

entries.name: Get-Service
entries.desc: Lists services and their state.
entries.equiv: CMD: sc query; Linux: systemctl list-units

entries.name: Restart-Service / Set-Service
entries.desc: Restarts a service or changes its startup type.
ex: net stop spooler && net start spooler
entries.pitfall: -Force also restarts dependent services. A disabled service no longer starts, even on demand.
entries.equiv: CMD: net stop/start, sc; Linux: systemctl restart

entries.name: Get-CimInstance Win32_Process
entries.desc: Processes with full command line and parent.
entries.equiv: CMD: wmic process get ...; Linux: ps -ef

entries.name: ipconfig
entries.desc: Shows the IP configuration and manages the DNS cache and DHCP lease.
entries.pitfall: /release cuts the connection; do not run it remotely. /all and /displaydns are read-only.
entries.equiv: PowerShell: Get-NetIPConfiguration, Clear-DnsClientCache; Linux: ip a, resolvectl flush-caches

entries.name: Test-NetConnection
entries.desc: Tests connectivity (ping, TCP port, route).
entries.pitfall: Tests TCP only; for a UDP port, use another tool. Blocked ICMP makes the ping fail while the port answers.
entries.equiv: CMD: ping, telnet; Linux: nc -zv, traceroute

entries.name: Get-NetAdapter
entries.desc: Lists network adapters, their state, speed and MAC address.
entries.pitfall: Restart-NetAdapter, Enable-/Disable-NetAdapter change the system (elevated prompt) and cut the connection.
entries.equiv: CMD: getmac, netsh interface show interface; Linux: ip link

entries.name: Get-NetIPAddress / Get-NetIPConfiguration
entries.desc: IP addresses, gateway and DNS of each interface.

entries.name: Resolve-DnsName
entries.desc: Queries DNS (A, MX, TXT, CNAME…) without nslookup.

entries.name: Get-NetTCPConnection
entries.desc: TCP connections and listening ports, with the owning process.

entries.name: netsh
entries.desc: Network configuration tool (Wi-Fi, firewall, proxy, stack reset).
ex: netsh wlan show profile name="MonWifi" key=clear
entries.perms: Elevated prompt to change (plain read needs no elevation, except key=clear)
entries.pitfall: winsock reset and int ip reset require a restart. key=clear shows a Wi-Fi password in clear text.
entries.equiv: PowerShell: NetAdapter, NetSecurity modules; Linux: nmcli, iptables

entries.name: ping / tracert / pathping
entries.desc: Tests reachability and the network path to a host.
entries.pitfall: Many firewalls block ICMP: a ping with no reply does not prove the host is down.

entries.name: Get-Disk / Get-Volume
entries.desc: Physical disks, partitions and volumes (size, free space, health).
entries.equiv: CMD: diskpart > list disk; Linux: lsblk, df -h

entries.name: Get-PhysicalDisk
entries.desc: Disk health state and reliability counters (simplified SMART).
entries.pitfall: A 'Healthy' state does not rule out an imminent failure: also watch Wear and read errors.

entries.name: cleanmgr / Storage Sense
entries.desc: Disk cleanup driven by a saved profile.
entries.pitfall: Windows 11 partly replaces cleanmgr with Storage Sense (Settings > System > Storage).

entries.name: diskpart
entries.syn: diskpart > list disk | select disk <n> | clean | create partition primary
entries.desc: Advanced management of disks and partitions in interactive mode.
entries.pitfall: 'clean' erases the whole partition table of the selected disk: double-check the number with list disk.
entries.equiv: PowerShell: Get-Disk, Initialize-Disk, New-Partition; Linux: fdisk, parted

entries.name: Get-LocalUser
entries.desc: Lists local accounts and their state.
entries.pitfall: Creating, enabling or changing an account needs an elevated prompt.
entries.equiv: CMD: net user; Linux: getent passwd

entries.name: Add-LocalGroupMember
entries.desc: Adds an account to a local group (for example Administrators).
entries.pitfall: The group name depends on Windows' language (Administrateurs / Administrators): use the SID S-1-5-32-544 to be language-independent.

entries.name: whoami
entries.desc: Shows the current user, their groups and privileges.
entries.pitfall: whoami /groups lets you check whether the session is elevated (high mandatory level).

entries.name: net user
entries.desc: Manages local user accounts (or domain accounts with /domain).
entries.pitfall: Typing the password on the command line leaves it in the history: prefer the prompt (*).
entries.equiv: PowerShell: Get-LocalUser, Get-ADUser; Linux: getent passwd

entries.name: manage-bde
entries.desc: BitLocker state and management on the command line.
entries.pitfall: Back up the recovery key (Entra ID, AD or Microsoft account) before encrypting or changing protectors.

entries.name: Get-BitLockerVolume
entries.desc: BitLocker encryption state and protectors of each volume.
entries.pitfall: Suspend-BitLocker should only be used temporarily (BIOS update) and resumes at the next restart.

entries.name: Get-MpComputerStatus / Start-MpScan
entries.desc: Microsoft Defender Antivirus state and starting a scan.
entries.pitfall: Get-MpComputerStatus is read-only; scanning and updating signatures change the state.

entries.name: gpupdate
entries.desc: Applies group policies immediately.
entries.pitfall: Some settings (software installation, startup scripts) need a restart or sign-in again (/logoff, /boot).

entries.name: gpresult
entries.desc: Shows the group policies actually applied to the machine and the user.
entries.pitfall: For the computer part, run it from an elevated prompt, otherwise the section is empty.

entries.name: Get-NetFirewallRule
entries.desc: Lists or creates Windows Defender Firewall rules.
entries.pitfall: Creating or changing a rule needs an elevated prompt and changes the machine's network exposure.
entries.equiv: CMD: netsh advfirewall; Linux: iptables, ufw

entries.name: Get-ExecutionPolicy / Set-ExecutionPolicy
entries.desc: The PowerShell script execution policy.
entries.pitfall: It is not a security boundary. Prefer -Scope CurrentUser over LocalMachine; Set-ExecutionPolicy changes the system.

entries.name: Get-WinEvent
entries.desc: Reads Windows event logs, with efficient filtering.
ex: Get-WinEvent -ListLog * | Where RecordCount -gt 0 | Sort RecordCount -Descending | Select -First 10 LogName,RecordCount
entries.perms: Elevated prompt for the Security log
entries.pitfall: Prefer -FilterHashtable to Where-Object: filtering happens at the source and stays fast on large logs.

entries.name: wevtutil
entries.desc: Queries, exports or clears an event log.
entries.perms: Elevated prompt to export or clear
entries.pitfall: wevtutil cl clears the log permanently: export it first with epl.

entries.name: Get-EventLog
entries.desc: Old reading of the classic logs (Windows PowerShell 5.1 only).
entries.pitfall: Missing from PowerShell 7: use Get-WinEvent.

entries.name: Get-CimInstance Win32_ReliabilityRecords
entries.desc: Reliability history (crashes, installation failures) as in Reliability Monitor.
ex: Get-CimInstance Win32_ReliabilityRecords | Where SourceName -eq 'Application Error' | Select TimeGenerated,ProductName,Message -First 10

entries.name: Reset-ComputerMachinePassword / Test-ComputerSecureChannel
entries.desc: Checks and repairs the trust relationship between the machine and the domain.
entries.perms: Elevated prompt and an authorized domain account
entries.pitfall: Message 'The trust relationship between this workstation and the primary domain failed': this is the quickest fix before rejoining the domain.

entries.name: dsregcmd /status
entries.desc: State of the Entra ID / hybrid join and of the authentication token (PRT).
entries.pitfall: AzureAdPrt: NO means a missing primary refresh token (broken SSO): sign in again or redo the join.

entries.name: Reset Windows Update (services and cache)
entries.syn: net stop wuauserv, bits ; rename SoftwareDistribution ; net start
entries.desc: Classic procedure when Windows Update stays stuck.
ex: net stop wuauserv && net stop bits
net start bits && net start wuauserv
entries.pitfall: The Windows Update history starts from zero. Try the troubleshooter and DISM /RestoreHealth first.

entries.name: powercfg /batteryreport
entries.desc: Battery report, energy diagnostics, and what prevents sleep.
entries.pitfall: /energy takes 60 seconds during which the PC must stay idle. /a lists the available sleep states.
